html:
Tsongkhapa was a Tibetan Buddhist monk and thinker who founded the Gelug school, the school to which the Dalai Lamas belong.

He was born in 1357 in Amdo, in northeastern Tibet, where the great Kumbum monastery later rose at his birthplace. As a young man he went to central Tibet and studied with teachers of many schools. He drew especially on the Kadam tradition that had grown from the teaching of Atisha.

He believed Tibetan Buddhism had grown lax. He stressed strict monastic rules, careful study and debate, and the Madhyamaka philosophy of Nagarjuna, before any practice of tantra. His great book, the Lamrim Chenmo (1402), sets out the stages of the path to enlightenment step by step.

  • In 1409 he founded the Great Prayer Festival at the Jokhang in Lhasa.
  • In the same year he founded Ganden monastery; this is the start of the Gelug school.
  • His students founded the great monasteries of Drepung and Sera near Lhasa.

One of his disciples was later counted as the first Dalai Lama. By the 17th century the Gelug had become the leading school in Tibet, and the 5th Dalai Lama ruled the country.
